newsitem.title: ITALY: Nuccio Bertone, doyen of Italian car design, dies.
newsitem.headline: Nuccio Bertone, doyen of Italian car design, dies.

text.p: Nuccio Bertone, one of the car world's great mentors and the doyen of Italian design, died on Wednesday at the age of 82, his company said in a statement.
Born in Turin on July 4, 1914, he entered his father's small coachworks firm in his early twenties, gradually transforming it into a fully-fledged industrial plant.
In more than 50 years of intense activity, Bertone became a world leader in the design and construction of niche vehicles.
He was responsible for the 1954 Alfa Romeo Giulietta Sprint, of which 40,000 were built against an expected 500, the Fiat 850 Spider and the Fiat X1/9.

The Bertone Lamborghinis are the hallmarks of an epoch -- the Miura, Espada and Countach each figuring as milestones in automotive history. Other masterpieces followed, like the Ferrari Dino 308 GT4 and the Lancia Stratos.
Finally in the 1990s, came the Citroens ZX and Xantia, the Opel Astra and Fiat Punto cabriolets and the Citroen Berlingo.
On May 22, 1995, came a Guinness Book of Records entry when the Bertone ZER blasted through the 300 km per hour (186 mph) barrier to achieve a record speed of 303.977 km/h (188.466 mph).

Bertone leaves two daughters who have followed their father's paths: Marie Jeanne, a graduate in architecture, oversees the creative section of the Bertone group, and Barbara, an economics graduate, the industrial production division.

Today the group employs 1,500 with revenues of 540 billion lire ($320 million). The group companies are Carrozzeria Bertone, Stile Bertone, Tecnodesign and Socar-Ics, all overseen by Chief Executive Officer Paolo Caccamo.
